episodes.176621: Radar indicated heavy rain across portions of Maui County through the early morning hours. The most intense rain fell over the Wailuku and Waikapu areas with rainfall rates of one to two inches per hour over saturated ground. The Maalaea area of south Maui and the Honoapiilani Highway from Maalaea to Lahaina were the most vulnerable to flooding impacts, as well poor drainage areas in Wailuku and Kahului. The Honopou Stream gage on the windward Haleakala slopes also showed rapid increase in water levels.
episodes.176658: Winter temperatures were the in the top 5 for coldest resulting in significant ice buildup on the Lemhi River. Cold temperatures culminated on January 30th with a low of -33F in Leadore and -18F in Salmon. Ice jam related flooding occurred around this significant cold period.
episodes.176989: Heavy rain brought river flooding to parts of Arkansas in late January. The Ouachita River and the White River were affected.
episodes.177264: A surface pressure trough, which later turned into a stationary front, situated over the Gulf of Mexico slowly crept northward until it reached the I-12 corridor near Baton Rouge. There, with abundant moisture in place, heavy showers developed along it as the front as it stalled right over Baton Rouge. Heavy downpours from stationary showers and storms produced flash flooding throughout the Baton Rouge metro and its surrounding suburbs on the morning of the 29th. By late-afternoon, the showers and storms finally weakened and dissipated, allowing the flooding to subside.
